gap_updates.rationale: No interval-applicable corridor control relation was found; Chester archaeology does not supply political authority and no second named locality qualified.
The only locatable Powys evidence remains a ninth-century retrospective inscription lineage, insufficient to bridge 780–796.
No named-place Gwynedd relation exists inside the interval; the 798 Caradog notice cannot be merged with the 796 Rhuddlan event.
The annal does not name parties or outcome, later assignments are conjectural, and no defensible exact battle coordinate exists.
Broad and conflicting dates do not jointly identify a target-interval section and independent political/traversal role; display-only remains binding.
Gobowen points to the early ninth century, Erddig remains imprecise, the legacy record conflicts, and no independent target-interval role is supported.
